notes: Introduced a modular Cyberdeck core registry/event bus under game.adk.cyberdeck
Moved Network Device definitions, scanning, persistence, security defaults, and discovery rules into FEHA_NETWORK_DEVICES.js
Added capability-driven device actions with d20 + INT modifier + proficiency breach checks against device Security DC
Successful device access is cached per actor/scene/device for the current session
Added real Foundry Door discovery and OPEN/CLOSE/LOCK/UNLOCK actions
Secret Foundry doors are not automatically exposed to non-GM users unless explicitly discovered
Tagged Tokens, Tiles, Walls, and AmbientLights can become Network Devices through flags.fleshEnshrouded.networkDevice
Added player PROBE mode for marking unknown devices on the cyber map
Added online GM approval queue where the GM chooses device type, label, and Security DC or denies the probe
Approved probe devices are persisted as Scene network records and discovered only by the requesting player until revealed
Player world mutations are delegated through online GM authority instead of relying on player Scene/Wall write permission
Terminals/System nodes can reveal hidden custom network devices to the requesting player
Network Device cards participate in JACK IN's existing collision fan-out and tether layout
Added isolated FEHA_CAMERA_FEEDS.js adapter instead of embedding camera behavior in JACK IN
Camera PLACE FEED enters a deliberately vague cyber-map placement mode
Camera feeds create client-local Foundry PointVisionSource POVs and temporarily suppress normal vision sources until RETURN TO NET
Multiple camera feeds persist for the current client session and can be cycled with PREV/NEXT
Camera POV has its own compromised-surveillance HUD and restores normal vision on return
Added HANDOFF/CYBERDECK_ARCHITECTURE_0.9.md as the authoritative anti-spaghetti module contract
Canonical loader now loads Cyber Core, Network Devices, Device Actions, Network Approvals, Camera Feeds, then V3 UI
Network Device Security DC now scales with access scope as well as device category
Added explicit access scopes: ENDPOINT (+0), LOCAL (+1), SUBSYSTEM (+2), BUILDING (+3), CORE (+5)
Typical defaults now resolve to: Lights 10, Camera 11, Door 12, Alarm 13, Turret 15, Terminal 17 (subsystem), System 19 (building)
GM approval queue now includes an ACCESS SCOPE selector and automatically recalculates the suggested DC
Changing device type resets to that type's normal scope, while the GM may freely override both scope and final DC
Persisted Network Device records now store accessScope/accessScopeLabel so JACK IN can show how broad the node's control is
JACK IN device nodes and device detail panels now display access scope alongside Security DC
Security remains fully GM-overridable, including DC 0 for unsecured devices and 20+ for exceptional hardened infrastructure
Fixed session Network Device access cache keys so colon-bearing IDs such as door:..., probe:..., and doc:... can be invalidated reliably
Player device command and reveal requests now fail fast when no online GM authority exists and time out cleanly if the authority path stops responding

GM-authoritative device command relay now revalidates the active requesting user, operator Actor ownership, device capability, discovery gating, and Secret Door visibility before mutating Foundry documents
Fixed JACK IN header grid mismatch that wrapped RETURN TO DECK / CLOSE CYBERDECK into an unintended second row
Reduced Quickhack execution dock height to recover more vertical space for the live network map
Increased real Scene underlay legibility while preserving the cyber treatment
Sparse one-endpoint scenes now use larger endpoint/operator decision surfaces without changing true token anchors
knownLimitations: Camera feed vision uses a client-local PointVisionSource and requires live Foundry testing to confirm final LOS/range behavior on the user's exact v14.361 client
Camera feeds are session-local in 0.9.1 and are not yet persisted across reconnects
Camera rotation/limited-angle behavior is not yet automated; the first adapter establishes a wall-aware point-of-view source
Turret ROTATE/FIRE still intentionally require a future turret adapter; generic DISABLE/ENABLE/TAKEOVER infrastructure is present
Status effects and non-damage Quickhack secondary effects are still not yet Active Effects
Quickhack rules still use effectText parsing as a legacy bridge pending explicit schema migration
The dev loader remains GM-only; player-client multiplayer device testing requires the modular runtime to be loaded through the actual FEHA module or an equivalent player-safe dev bootstrap
